title: Gram Nyayalayas
lead: Village-level courts under the ==Gram Nyayalayas Act, 2008== — meant to bring ==affordable, accessible and speedy justice to rural citizens at their doorstep==.

items: ==Establishment==: State governments, ==in consultation with the High Court==, for every intermediate panchayat or group of contiguous panchayats
==Appointment==: the presiding officer — ==Nyayadhikari== — appointed by the state government in consultation with the HC; must qualify as a ==Judicial Magistrate First Class==
==Jurisdiction==: both civil and criminal, per the First and Second Schedules — property and labour disputes; ==criminal offences punishable up to 2 years==
==Procedure==: simplified; ==not bound by the Evidence Act== (now Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam), guided by ==natural justice== and HC rules
==Conciliation==: civil disputes must ==first be attempted through conciliation==
==Appeals==: criminal to the Court of Session, civil to the District Court — ==strict 6-month disposal timeline==

items.label: operational in states like Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
of 4,20,129 cases received since 2020 disposed of to date

items.title: Global Best Practices
bullets: ==Gacaca courts in Rwanda== and African informal justice systems — ==community participation and reconciliation==
==UK and Canada== — simplified procedures for ==small claims and minor offences==
==South Africa and Indonesia== — community-based systems ==integrated with the formal judiciary== for oversight and rights protection

items: ==A regular cadre of Nyayadhikaris== — continuity and professionalism
==Permanent infrastructure== with adequate staff and resources
==Clear jurisdiction== to avoid overlap with other forums

blocks.text: Gram Nyayalayas were meant to bring justice to the doorstep — but without proper funding, staffing and awareness, they remain courts in name, not in reach.
